messages:
maya: heads up — during tenant onboarding in staging I'm seeing repeated SCIM 403s for service accounts after the RBAC cleanup deploy. externalId is coming back empty for some entries.
jess: Which deploy? can you paste the error snippet and the provisioning payload?
maya: rolled the role-mapping change at 09:11. logs show: `scim: provision failed status=403 body=\"forbidden: access denied\" externalId=\"\"`. Also seeing KMS decrypt errors in the provisioner: `kms: decrypt failed: context mismatch for key alias/redwood-provisioner`
samir: ugh, context mismatch usually means the encryption context we used for wrapping extid changed. Did the RBAC change include a principal rename that would change extid generation?
maya: possible — role names were normalized (lowercased + strip domain). service-account externalId is generated from `svc/${tenant}/${role}`. Rolename normalization might produce a different string compared to the wrapped context.
leo: quick check: can you dump a failing `encrypted_extid` header (base64) and prefix the open-source decrypt util? don't paste keys, just the ciphertext and envelope header.
maya: pasted to the secure log channel: `envhdr: alg=A256GCM, ctx=")tenant=acme;svc=payments;role=BillingAdmin("` ciphertext truncated...
jess: that ctx looks like it still has old casing and parentheses? formatting seems off. we recently removed the legacy NameQualifier from SAML, so SCIM mapper might be falling back to legacy path.
samir: If the encryption context used during wrap contains the original role string, and our unwrap uses the normalized role, KMS will reject it due to context mismatch. We need to either rewrap with the normalized ctx or make unwrap accept both contexts (not ideal).
security-bot: [vuln-triage] flagged: potential broken access control for onboarded service accounts. Assign severity=S1 if customers affected.
maya: mitigation in staging: reverted the role normalization in the deploy; started a small re-onboard job that rewraps extids with the old ctx. That cleared ~70% of failing accounts.
leo: good temporary step. Long term we should run a controlled rewrap that canonicalizes to the new format and update downstream caches. Also need to update audit logs to record which ctx was used for wrap/unwrap for future forensics.
jess: agree. Also we should check SAML NameID format changes — I found a couple assertions with NameID Format=transient and NameQualifier dropped. Snippet:
<saml:NameID Format=\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress\">svc-payments@example.com</saml:NameID>
Some downstream mappers expect `idp.entityId + ":" + NameID` and now it's just NameID.
samir: that matches failing correlation: SCIM provisioning expects `externalId = idp-entity|nameid|role`. if NameQualifier goes away we lose `idp-entity` prefix and encryption context differs.
maya: action items: 1) run a full rewrap job in staging to regenerate extids with the canonical context, 2) add a compatibility unwrap path for a 48h window, 3) roll a light audit event whenever wrap/unwrap occurs including ctx fingerprint, 4) create a postmortem draft.
jess: I'll open a short rollback incident for production gating and notify support. ping @oncall if any tenant onboarding in prod fails.
ops-bot: deployed rollback of role-normalization at 09:23 — canary passed.
security-bot: reminder: coordinate KMS key rotation window with SRE before rewrapping. key rotation + rewrap out of order will cause large-scale failures.
leo: also add an eval to Redwood Optimize to detect extid drift on onboarding flows — quick metric: ratio of empty externalId per 1k provisioning events.
samir: for the postmortem please include timeline, root cause (ctx derived from role canonicalization), mitigations, and a permanent fix (wrap contract change + audit).
maya: I'll paste initial notes into the incident doc and include sample logs and the small repro script I used.
jess: thanks — please tag the incident with affected tenants list when available.
maya: will do. closing loop in ~2h after the rewrap run completes. :white_check_mark:
